title: Iki run output (iki/v1)
description: What an action's command writes to output.json: the entities it changes and creates, within what its action declares. Iki writes all of it in one transaction, or none of it.

origin.description: Where an imported entity came from: a public database, or a file the run was given. Iki keeps it with the entity, for anyone who reads it.

source.description: The database or format, such as `NCBI Nucleotide`, `RCSB PDB` or `GenBank file`.

id.description: Its identifier there: an accession, or a record's name in a file.

version.description: The record's version or the database's release, such as `L09137.2` or `2026-11`.

url.description: Where people can see the record.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the record as the command read it.

file.description: The file it was read from: one of the run's file params.

made.description: How the source says it made the entity, as its record states it, never guessed: from mmCIF's `_exptl` and `_software`, say, or ModelCIF's `_ma_` categories. Iki shows it as the source's statement, not its own record (ADR 0106).

kind.description: Measured, such as by X-ray diffraction, or computed, such as predicted by a model.

method.description: The method as the source names it, such as `X-RAY DIFFRACTION`.

software.description: The tools it says made it, such as AlphaFold 2.3.2.

details.description: What else it states about the making, by name, such as a model's mean pLDDT.

create.description: A new entity, of a type the action declares it creates.

type.description: Its type, by its qualified name, such as `iki/protein.Protein`.

key.description: A name for it, unique in `creates`, that a later create's ref fields can give as `{"$create": "<key>"}` to refer to it, such as a structure to the chains made with it. Not in a `creates_file`.

values.description: Its fields' values. A ref field (or an item of a list of refs) may be `{"$create": "<key>"}`: the entity an earlier create with that key made or reused.

derived_from.description: The input entities it was made from. Leave it out when the declared inputs it's derived from hold one entity (never in a job that runs several runs at once: see `pack` in input.json).

made_with.description: Which of the action's `software` made it, by name, when the action lists more than one and the run chose. Leave it out to mean all of them (ADR 0106).

updates.description: By input name (one the action declares it updates): the entities it was given there, and the new values of fields the action declares.

entity.description: The input entity's ID, from input.json.

creates.description: New entities, of types the action declares it creates.

creates_file.description: Creates too many for output.json (over 10,000, or large ones): a file in IKI_OUT_DIR with one create per line, each as an item of `creates` is (JSON Lines). Iki checks every line, then writes them all or none, as it does `creates`. Their values can't attach files. Give `creates` or this, not both.

$file.description: The file's path in IKI_OUT_DIR, such as `creates.ndjson`.

anyOf.description: The file's ID, once the worker has uploaded it.

park.description: Wait on an outside API's job without holding a worker (ADR 0130): the API (one of the action's, with `jobs`), the job's ID as the API gave it, and what to pick up from. Iki polls the job, and once it's done runs the command again with `resume` in its input.json. Nothing is written now: give no `creates`, `creates_file` or `updates` with it.

job.description: The API's ID for the job.

state.description: Up to 64 KiB of JSON the command wants back when it resumes, such as which entity the job is for.

metrics.description: Numbers about the run, such as a score or a count, kept on the run.

messages.description: Notes for whoever reads the run.

entity.description: The input entity it's about, from input.json. A job that runs several runs of a batch at once gives each run the messages about its entity, and those about none. An `error` about an entity fails its run, which then writes nothing: a command can fail one entity and go on with the rest.
